name: Submerge
desc: The frame is put under water — a caustic net rakes down from a surface undulating overhead, suspended haze scatters the light into a body you can see through, and depth eats the red out of everything first so the bottom of the picture sinks away blue, whether that is a sunlit shallow, a dark deep, green silt, hard chlorine or the underside of ice.

energy.doc: how much light is in the water — caustic strength and overall emission

scale.doc: caustic cell size: 0.3 is a fine tight net, 2.4 is broad slow lobes of light

density.doc: turbidity — suspended matter hazing the water and catching the light

depth.doc: how fast colour is absorbed with distance down — the depth cue (red goes first, then green)

sharp.doc: caustic focus: 0 is soft diffuse lobes, 1 is hard bright veins

hue.doc: water colour (192 = clear sea); also steers which channel survives the depth

speed.doc: how fast the surface works and the light churns

y.doc: the waterline — 0.8 puts the surface just above frame, 1 brings it down into view

alpha.doc: master opacity of the whole pass

style.doc: which body of water — these change the physics (caustic focus, absorption, turbidity, what the ceiling is), not just the hue

act.doc: multi-minute program: an even drift, a chop that builds and eases, or a slow descent into the dark
